_comment: Baked by scripts/bake_updates.py from hebrish.app/changelog; do not edit by hand. Shown offline in the apps' What's new (Android Updates screen, desktop About tab).

entries.title: Windows and AppImage catch up
entries.summary: The same app as 1.047 (fewer invented phrases from silence and breaths), now also as the Windows installer and the AppImage.

entries.title: Fewer invented phrases from silence and breaths
entries.summary: A recording with no speech in it, or the very first moment of one, could come back as a phrase nobody said. Hebrish now remembers how loud you usually speak into each microphone and skips a piece that is far quieter than that and holds almost no speech.

entries.title: Acknowledgements: the Jerusalem Municipality
entries.summary: The acknowledgements page now credits the Jerusalem Municipality's GIS department for the city's street names and their official English spellings.

entries.title: Maintainer mode is now called Ticked, with its own tab on Ubuntu
entries.summary: Ticked is the new name for maintainer mode: the switch that keeps each Voice Typing take's recording beside its History row, with the storage used, the capacity and how many days to keep them.

entries.title: A Maintainer tab for keeping the audio of your takes
entries.summary: Settings now has a Maintainer tab: switch maintainer mode on to keep each Voice Typing take's recording beside its History row, see how much disk the recordings use right now in gigabytes, and set the capacity and how many days to keep them.

entries.title: Acknowledgements: the data supporters behind the names and places
entries.summary: A new acknowledgements page credits the organisations and people who gave data, recordings and help, with what each contributed: the Central Bureau of Statistics (first-name birth counts), data.gov.il at the National Digital Agency (the national street list and the Population…

entries.title: A web page you choose can start and stop dictation
entries.summary: Web pages allowed (Settings, Local API; empty unless you fill it in): list a site, and a page on it can show whether Hebrish is recording and start or stop dictation, so it can have its own mic button.

entries.title: Windows gets an installer that keeps Hebrish up to date
entries.summary: Windows now installs with a normal installer: for your user only, no admin rights, with Start menu and desktop shortcuts and an uninstaller.

entries.title: Model downloads survive a dropped connection
entries.summary: A model download that loses its connection or times out no longer fails: it waits, retries and carries on from where it stopped.

entries.title: Change settings through the local API
entries.summary: New GET and POST /v1/app/settings: read and change the everyday settings (outputs, paste and send shortcuts, pane and window binding, Enter after silence, pacing, sounds, voice detection) from a script or an AI agent.

entries.title: Dictation goes where you started it, even if you move to another pane or window
entries.summary: A take remembers the Konsole pane it started in. Its text and its Enter go there even after you click into another pane, so dictating into one of several terminals split side by side no longer lands in the wrong one.

entries.title: Dictate in Hebrew: a Hebrew-only model, used when your keyboard layout is Hebrew
entries.summary: A new Hebrew model writes in Hebrew letters. With it downloaded, Voice Typing uses it when your keyboard layout is Hebrew; English stays on your main model.

entries.title: Meorav-Multi-Voice: voice names and avatars, a proof-of-concept label, and how it was trained
entries.summary: The five voices of Meorav-Multi-Voice have names and illustrated avatars: Josh (American male, the same designed voice as Meorav v3.0), Rivka (American female), Nigel (British male), Fiona (British female) and Bazza (Australian male).

entries.title: Ubuntu 1.035: A warning when the microphone hears nothing; quiet model updates
entries.summary: Silence guard: if a recording has run for 10 seconds and the microphone hasn't picked up any sound at all (muted, unplugged or the wrong input), Hebrish shows a warning notification, so you don't dictate into nothing.

entries.title: Ubuntu 1.034: Models in a window of their own
entries.summary: Models has its own window, opened from the new Models button at the top of the main window, or from the tray. It was a tab inside Settings.

entries.title: Ubuntu 1.033: No full stop at the end, and a live draft
entries.summary: No full stop at the end: a new switch, in Settings and in the tray under Output, leaves off the final full stop of each take.

entries.title: Ubuntu 1.032: Stop transcribes, and the Notepad gets formatting
entries.summary: Stop now transcribes. On the Transcription tab, the square Stop button stops the recording and puts the transcript in the Notepad.

entries.title: Ubuntu 1.031: Settings in their own window, Transcription as a Notepad
entries.summary: The main window holds the modes: Voice Typing, Transcription and History. Settings, Models, Dictionary, Updates, Diagnostics and About open in a separate Settings window, from the buttons at the top or Settings… in the tray menu.

entries.title: Ubuntu 1.030: Enter waits for the last words
entries.summary: Send pressed early: Hold the send key until they're in now also covers an Enter pressed while you're still recording (with The send key stops recording on).

entries.title: Falafel: the third model in active development
entries.summary: Falafel, the voice-command model, has its own page and sits beside Sabich and Shakshuka on /models and the home page. Two sizes, Falafel (desktop) and Falafel 110M (phones and laptop CPUs).
